caption: An axe swung down onto a log standing on end on a chopping block splits it into two pieces that fall apart to the sides.

sa.check: A log stands on end on a chopping block.
An axe is swung down onto it.
The log splits into two pieces.
The pieces fall apart to the sides.
The log stands on end before the blow.
The blow comes first, then the split, then the halves fall.

pc.expect: The split starts where the blade bites and runs down the log with a rough grain face.
pc.fail: The axe passes through with no effect; or the log squashes; or the split is a clean smooth cut.

pc.expect: The halves fall away only after the blow lands, outward to the sides.
pc.fail: The halves fall before the blow; or both fall to the same side; or they fly upward.

pc.expect: The halves fall to the ground, and the axe stays in the block or is lifted.
pc.fail: The halves hang in the air; or rise; or the axe floats.
It slides; or jumps; or the log moves before the blow.

pc.expect: One log becomes two pieces and one axe keeps its number.
pc.fail: A third piece appears; or a half vanishes; or the axe vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The log's bark, the axe and the yard stay the same.
pc.fail: The bark changes; or the axe changes; or the yard rearranges.

note: The person swinging is kept because the swing is the physics. Technique is not judged.
